title: Derived completion computes infinitesimal punctured-spectrum cohomology
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, let $M$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and put $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathcal F=\widetilde M|_U$ be the associated sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Work in the ordinary derived category $D(A)$ of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an ideal $K$, put $\Gamma_K(N)=\{x\in N:K^r x=0\text{ for some }r\geq0\}$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], and write $R\Gamma_K$ for its right derived functor and $H_K^j(M)=H^j(R\Gamma_K(M[0]))$. Write $L^{\wedge_I}=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n)$ for derived $I$-adic completion: the derived tensor is computed using a K-flat resolution, and the derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] using the mapping fibre of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the termwise products of a complex-level model of the tower. Use these derived-functor models and their natural completion maps, not arbitrary maps between abstract choices of cones. Write $R\Gamma(U,-)$ for derived global sections of Zariski module sheaves [pqf-def-cohomology]. For every integer $i$ there is a canonical isomorphism $H^i((R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F))^{\wedge_I})\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}H^i(U,\widetilde{M/I^nM}|_U)$. It is natural in $M$ and is induced by reduction maps; its composite with the completion map from $H^i(U,\mathcal F)$ has $n$th coordinate the map induced by $M\to M/I^nM$. Negative Zariski cohomology groups are understood to be zero. Moreover, for every open $V\subseteq U$ there is likewise a canonical isomorphism $H^0((R\Gamma(V,\mathcal F|_V))^{\wedge_I})\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\Gamma(V,\widetilde{M/I^nM}|_V)$ (for $V=U$ the one above with $i=0$), natural in $M$, whose composite with the completion map from $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F|_V)$ has $n$th coordinate the map induced by $M\to M/I^nM$; for opens $V'\subseteq V\subseteq U$ these isomorphisms carry $H^0$ of the completed restriction map $(R\Gamma(V,\mathcal F|_V))^{\wedge_I}\to(R\Gamma(V',\mathcal F|_{V'}))^{\wedge_I}$ to the limit of the restriction maps.

source.place: Tag 0DXI, lemma-compare-with-derived-completion, applied to the restriction of the sheaf associated to a finite module; its proof uses Tag 0DX1 (lemma-ML-local) and Tag 0A0K (lemma-derived-completion-pseudo-coherent). The degree-zero clause for an open V of U is the same proof on V (Tags 0BLX, lemma-formal-functions-general, and 0D60, cohomology-lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim), where the R^1lim term involves H^{-1}=0 and no Mittag-Leffler input is needed.

proof.text: Put $M_n=M/I^nM$ and $\mathcal F_n=\widetilde{M_n}|_U$. The tilde sheaf is quasi-coherent. Finite generators of $M$ (respectively $M_n$) generate its localizations, hence the associated sheaf is of finite type. The scheme $U$, and every open $V\subseteq U$, is locally Noetherian. Thus [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes these restrictions coherent. On $D(f)\subseteq U$, localization gives $M_f/I^nM_f\cong(M/I^nM)_f$: the quotient sends $m/f^k$ to $\bar m/f^k$; its kernel consists of fractions with a power of $f$ times the numerator in $I^nM$, exactly $I^nM_f$. The identification commutes with further localization and reduction in $n$, so it sheafifies to $\mathcal F/I^n\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F_n$ and restricts to any $V$.

source.place: Tag 0DXI, preliminary identification of coherent reductions; coherence criterion Tag 01XZ

proof.text: Let $\Lambda_A$ and $\Lambda_U$ denote the intrinsic derived-completion reflections on the one-point ringed site $(pt,A)$ and on $(U,\mathcal O_U)$ with ideals $I$ and $I\mathcal O_U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] on the one-point site: its quotient/Koszul unit comparison identifies $\Lambda_A L$ with $L^{\wedge_I}=R\varprojlim_n(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n)$ for every $L\in D(A)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pushforward-completion] to the structure morphism $(U,\mathcal O_U)\to(pt,A)$; the resulting unit-normalized isomorphism gives $(R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F))^{\wedge_I}\cong R\Gamma(U,\Lambda_U\mathcal F)$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated and $I\mathcal O_U$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal. The coherent-sheaf clause of [lem-per-derived-completion-pseudocoherent] and Step 1 identify $\Lambda_U\mathcal F$ with $R\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n$. The comparisons carry the completion unit to the quotient maps, so the composite to the $n$th projection is induced by $M\to M_n$.

source.place: Tag 0DXI, first displayed equality: Tag 0BLX is the structure-morphism case of Tag 0A0G; Tag 0A0K identifies the coherent-sheaf model. The module model is the one-point specialization of the existing constant-completion comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-ringed-space-rgamma-derived-limit] to the tower $\mathcal F_n$ on the ringed space $U$. For every integer $i$ its Milnor sequence, after Step 2, is $$0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{i-1}(U,\mathcal F_n)\to H^i((R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F))^{\wedge_I})\to\varprojlim_n H^i(U,\mathcal F_n)\to0.$$ The right map is induced by the projections of the chosen derived-functor limit model. In particular its composite with the completion map has the reduction coordinates computed in Step 2.

For $j>0$, the coherent-sheaf clause of [lem-per-punctured-cohomology-ml] applied to $\mathcal F_n$ makes $(H^j(U,\mathcal F_n))_n$ Mittag-Leffler. For $j<0$ it is the zero tower by the negative-cohomology convention. It remains to verify degree zero; no arbitrary-tower degree-zero assertion is being used.

source.place: Tag 0DXI, last paragraph, positive-degree case from Tag 0DX1

proof.text: For $j=0$, take degree-zero cohomology of the natural localization triangle [lem-per-affine-support-cech-localization] with $K=\mathfrak m$ and $L=M_n[0]$. Since $H^1(M_n[0])=0$, it gives a natural exact sequence $M_n\to B_n\xrightarrow{p_n} C_n\to0$, where $B_n=H^0(U,\mathcal F_n)$ and $C_n=H^1_{\mathfrak m}(M_n)$. Put $Q_n=\operatorname{im}(M_n\to B_n)$. All maps $Q_m\to Q_n$ for $m\geq n$ are surjective, since $M_m\to M_n$ is surjective. Consequently $\operatorname{im}(B_m\to B_n)=p_n^{-1}(\operatorname{im}(C_m\to C_n))$: lift a preimage in $C_m$ to $B_m$, then correct its image by an element of $Q_m$ lifting the difference in $Q_n$. The first clause of [lem-per-punctured-cohomology-ml] makes the images in $C_n$ stabilize. The displayed equality makes the images in $B_n$ stabilize. Thus the degree-zero tower is Mittag-Leffler.

source.place: Tag 0DXI, degree-zero detail of its last paragraph, from Tag 0DX1 (1) and the localization triangle underlying Tag 0DWR (2)

proof.text: For every integer $i$, Steps 4 and 5 show that $(H^{i-1}(U,\mathcal F_n))_n$ is Mittag-Leffler. Apply [lem-per-mittag-leffler-derived-limit-acyclic] to kill the left term of Step 3. The resulting right-map isomorphism is the asserted one. Naturality in $M$ follows by applying the functorial comparisons to the commuting reduction maps of a homomorphism $M\to M'$. Its composite with the completion map has the specified coordinates by Step 3.

For any open $V\subseteq U$, repeat Step 2 with the structure morphism $(V,\mathcal O_V)\to(pt,A)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pushforward-completion], and [lem-per-derived-completion-pseudocoherent]. Apply [lem-pc-ringed-space-rgamma-derived-limit] in degree zero to $\mathcal F_n|_V$. Its left term $R^1\varprojlim_n H^{-1}(V,\mathcal F_n|_V)$ is zero, so its right map gives the required isomorphism, with the same reduction coordinates. For $V'\subseteq V$, the sheaf completion comparisons commute with restriction. The remaining square comparing completed sections with sections of the completed sheaf commutes by the reflection property: its target $R\Gamma(V',\Lambda_{V'}\mathcal F|_{V'})$ is derived complete over $A$ by the ringed-pushforward theorem, and after precomposition with the completion unit both arrows are restriction followed by the sheaf completion unit. Uniqueness of factorization through the left-adjoint reflection makes these arrows equal. The Milnor right maps commute with restriction since their $n$th coordinates are the projection maps. This proves the required inverse-limit restriction square, naturality in $M$, and the completion-to-reduction assertion. For $V=U$ it is exactly the right map of Step 3 in degree zero.
